The test image shows a corn stalk (not a leaf), tan/straw-colored and dried, with small dark specks/particles scattered on the surface. This looks like a stalk disease. Top candidates: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose.

Let me check reference images across multiple classes.
This Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference is extremely similar to the test image - same angle, same stalk, same background. Let me confirm with more references.
Strong match - small dark specks (pycnidia) on stalk surface. Let me check a few more classes to rule out alternatives.
Physoderma shows green stalk with dark bands (not matching). Anthracnose shows dark/reddish discoloration (not matching). Diplodia_Stalk_Rot remains top candidate. Let me check more classes.
Need to reach 16 different classes. Let me check 2 more.

All three Diplodia_Stalk_Rot references (Corn_Disease_14, 20, 28) show the same pattern as the test image: dried tan/straw-colored stalk with small dark pycnidia specks on the surface, in a dried corn field setting. No other class matches this presentation.

- Charcoal_Stalk_Rot: shows internal shredded tissue, no exterior speck pattern
- Physoderma_Stalk_Rot: green stalk with banded dark spots
- Anthracnose: reddish-dark stalk coloring
- Bacterial_Stalk_Rot: green wilting tissue
- All leaf diseases (rust, blight, spots, mosaic): clearly on leaf tissue, not stalks

Diplodia_Stalk_Rot is the clear match based on visual similarity.
